parts.problem_md: For a named tropical rainforest you have studied, describe and explain the characteristics of its natural vegetation.
parts.solution_md:
In the Amazon rainforest, plants grow in layers. Emergent trees, such as the kapok tree, are the tallest at 40 metres. **[KU]** The canopy is found at 30 metres, then the under canopy is at 20 metres.  The shrub layer is closest to the ground. **[KU] **Trunks are straight, and branches only appear higher up in the tree** ****[KU]**** **because this is where the leaves can reach the sunlight. **[KU]** The bark is smooth and thin so that rainwater can run off quickly. **[KU]**  Plants are evergreen because the climate allows year-round growth. **[KU]**

The leaves of plants have drip tips **[KU]** to shed excess water so the leaves do not break.  The emergent trees have large roots called 'buttress roots'** ****[KU]** to help support them.  Some plants, known as epiphytes, grow on trees higher up to reach sunlight, as it is too dark in the shrub layer. **[KU] **Some plants have bendy stems that allow them to follow the sun.  The leaves on plants in the shrub layer are broad enough to catch as much sun as possible. **[KU]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is '**explain**'  means that the answer needs to describe the vegetation characteristics and outline how this means they are suited to the rainforest.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> AO focus = AO1** ****[KU]**
> 
> - A top-level 3 **[7 marks]** answer will include specific examples that show:
> 
>   - Knowledge of the vegetation characteristics
>   - Understanding of how this shows their adaptations to the rainforest
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - Lianas use the tall trees to reach the sunlight

parts.problem_md: Explain why tropical rainforests are found close to the equator.
parts.solution_md:
The temperature at the equator is constant **[1]** all year at 27 degrees Celsius, and so this means plants can grow for twelve months of the year.**[1]** The area also receives lots of sunlight**,** which helps plants grow.**[1]**  Rainfall is 2000mm/year **[1]**and this is important for photosynthesis to occur and means that plants have water all year.  In tropical rainforests, the air is humid and this also encourages plant growth.**[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word 'explain' means that the answer should include supporting details and explanations for the reason vegetation growth is fast
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - **One mark** for each simple point
> - **One mark** for each development of the simple point
> 
> **[5 marks]**
> 
> Answers can be either:
> 
> - Five simple points
> - One developed point plus three simple points
> - Two points which are developed plus one simple point

parts.problem_md:
For a named area of **tropical rainforest** you have studied, describe the impacts of deforestation on the **local** natural environment.

Name of area ............................................
parts.solution_md:
Levels marking | **Level 1 (1–3 marks)** | **Level 2 (4–6 marks)** | **Level 3 (7 marks)** | |---|---|---| | Statements including limited detail which describe the impacts of deforestation on the local natural environment. | Uses named example.

More developed statements which describe the impacts of deforestation on the local natural environment. (NB Max 5 if no named or inappropriate example) | Comprehensive and accurate statements including some place specific reference. | Content Guide: Answers are likely to refer to: Loss of biodiversity Loss of habitat Extinction of species Impacts on food chain/ecosystems Soil erosion Leaching Increased overland flow Flooding etc. Place specific reference is likely to consist of: Locational details, Named places Specific details of loss of species Statistics etc. Place specific detail - *Locational details - Malaysia* - *Specific details -* - *Almost 70% of Malaysia is covered by tropical rainforest* - *It is estimated that Malaysia has the fastest rate of deforestation in the world* - *Since 2000 an average of over 140,000 hectares of forest has been felled and cleared each year* - *Examples of paragraphs which could be included in an answer to achieve Level 3:* - *Deforestation has a range of impacts many of which are* *environmental. Areas that have been deforested are often planted with monoculture which reduces habitats and therefore reduces biodiversity and can lead to the extinction of species. Palm oil plantations in Malaysia have lead to a 35% reduction in species, orangutans, pygmy elephants, Sumatran Rhino and Malayan tigers are all endangered. Deforestation also leads to interception and infiltration decreasing which reduces evapotranspiration and as a result precipitation decreases* - *Deforestation also increases overland flow this leads to soil erosion because the land is bare and exposed to the heavy rainfall which occurs in the rainforest. The soil then washes into the rivers leading to sedimentation which decreases their capacity because sediment builds up on riverbeds reducing their capacity and increasing the flood risk* - *Deforestation leads to local climate change because reduced transpiration and evaporation leads to a decrease in precipitation and an increase in temperatures. This means that rainfall patterns become less reliable and more extreme* - *Remember that the question specifies the local natural environment. This means that answers referring to global climate change will not be awarded marks nor will impacts on local people *

parts.problem_md:

parts.solution_md:
Levels marking | **Level 1 (1–3 marks)** | **Level 2 (4–6 marks)** | **Level 3 (7 marks)** | |---|---|---| | Statements including limited detail which explain why deforestation of tropical rainforests threatens the **global natural** environment. | Uses named example Developed or linked statements which explain why deforestation of tropical rainforests threatens the **global natural** environment.

(Note: Max 5 if no named or inappropriate example.) | Comprehensive and accurate statements including one reference to a place impacted. | Content Guide: Causes and/or impacts. Impacts must be **global natural** environment Answers are likely to include the following ideas: Less carbon dioxide used by trees Build up of Carbon dioxide/created by burning Forms layer/blanket Increase in temperatures/greenhouse effect/global warming Melting ice/glaciers Loss of species which live in impacted area e.g. polar bears Rising sea level Flooding of coastal lowlands, Loss of mangroves Changes to climatic patterns, e.g. drought etc. Place reference is likely to consist of: Names of places threatened E.g. Antarctica, Maldives, Alps, Andes Place specific detail - *Locational details - Antarctica, Arctic and Maldives* - *Specific details - * - *Increase in rate of ice melting in Antarctica - 150 billion tons a year* - *In Greenland 270 billion tons a year lost* - *Maldives predicted by one study to be uninhabitable by 2050* - *Examples of paragraphs which could be included in an answer to achieve Level 3:* - *Deforestation leads to a significant reduction in the number of trees. This means that less CO**2** is taken in by the trees as part of photosynthesis. This increases carbon dioxide concentrations in the atmosphere and as this is a greenhouse gas this increases human induced climate change. Use of fire for clearance also increases carbon dioxide emissions* - *Global warming has increased the average global temperature leading to increased melting of areas in the Arctic and Antarctic with a loss of 150 billion tons of ice melting per year. The rising sea levels threatens island nations such as the Maldives which some predictions state will be uninhabitable by 2050 if sea levels continue to rise at the current rate * - *Remember that the question specifies the global environment this means that reference to the impacts on local people or local natural environment will not be awarded marks*

parts.problem_md:

parts.solution_md:
Levels marking

| **Level 1 (1–3 marks)** | **Level 2 (4–6 marks)** | **Level 3 (7 marks)** |
|---|---|---|
| Statements including limited detail which describe the impacts of deforestation. | More developed or linked statements which describe the impacts of deforestation. | Comprehensive and accurate statements which describe the impacts of deforestation including place references, including named place(s). |

<u>Content Guide:</u>

Impact on people or natural environment 
Answers are likely to refer to: 
Soil erosion, 
Loss of biodiversity, 
Loss of habitat, 
Extinction of species, 
Increase in likelihood of flooding, 
Loss of land for indigenous peoples, 
Medicines

<u>Place specific detail</u>

- *Locational details - Malaysia*
- *Specific details -*

  - *Almost 70% of Malaysia is covered by tropical rainforest*
  - *It is estimated that Malaysia has the fastest rate of deforestation in the world*
  - *Since 2000 an average of over 140,000 hectares of forest has been felled and cleared each year*

- *Examples of paragraphs which could be included in an answer to achieve Level 3:*

  - *Deforestation has a range of impacts many of which are* *environmental. Areas that have been deforested are often planted with monoculture which reduces habitats and therefore reduces biodiversity and can lead to the extinction of species. Palm oil plantations in Malaysia have lead to a 35% reduction in species, orangutans, pygmy elephants, Sumatran Rhino and Malayan tigers are all endangered. Deforestation also leads to interception and infiltration decreasing which reduces evapotranspiration and as a result precipitation decreases*
  - *Deforestation also increases overland flow this leads to soil erosion because the land is bare and exposed to the heavy rainfall which occurs in the rainforest. The soil then washes into the rivers leading to sedimentation which decreases their capacity because sediment builds up on riverbeds reducing their capacity and increasing the flood risk*
  - *Deforestation means that indigenous communities* *such as the **Orang Asli and Temiar** have been forced off land. In addition the pollination of fruits has reduced due to a decrease in pollinating insects and animals such as bats which has reduced the available food sources. In Kuala Koh village 2019 at least 15 indigenous **Batek** died after an outbreak of disease possibly transmitted by loggers working near to the village*
- *Remember that the question specifies local people and local natural environment. This means that answers referring to global climate change will not be awarded marks*
